periods.analysis: We are starting this run in a mostly sound position: Water Main Breaks are 13.8 breaks/100mi, Unplanned Outage Minutes are 38 minutes, and Non-Revenue Water is 11%, all inside target. That is not luck; Crew 2 kept the 16-inch ductile iron on Airport Loop WM-16-044 valved and back in service before the terminal pressure zone saw a customer outage. The watch item is coastal hydraulics: Tidal & Storm Flooding Events are 26 days on a rolling-year basis against a target of <=20 days, so the yellow rating belongs to drainage and tide gates, not the water plant. The pipes are behaving, but the tide is keeping score.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green water results by keeping the Tuesday acoustic leak run on the Harborline and Seaport pressure districts and adding the two airport-fed DMAs to the same route. Move tide-gate inspections at Outfalls OF-7, OF-12, and OF-19 from quarterly to monthly through king-tide season, with photos and actuator readings attached to the work orders. Bring a short funding note to the next CIP review tying the 26 days to pump runtime and street-closure hours, because budget asks land better with units.

periods.analysis: The quarter-over-quarter direction is a little less comfortable but still controlled on the water side: Water Main Breaks moved from 13.8 to 14.2 breaks/100mi, Unplanned Outage Minutes from 38 to 40 minutes, and Non-Revenue Water from 11% to 11.1%. Those are green results, and the maintenance logs show the night crew avoided three full shutdowns by using line stops on WM-08-117 near Bayfront Avenue. The yellow condition persists because Tidal & Storm Flooding Events increased from 26 to 28 days, with nuisance flooding clustering along Dock Street and the low block of Mariners Way. In plain terms, the water system is still within spec, while the drainage system is absorbing more coastal days than the design book assumed.
periods.recommendations: Hold the valve-exercising schedule at 110 valves per month and prioritize the Harborline isolation valves that let crews keep outage minutes under 45. Extend leak detection one mile inland from the seaport grid before winter demand drops mask small leaks. For flooding, stage temporary pump P-4 at Dock Street before forecast tides above 6.8 feet and have Engineering price the flap-gate retrofit for OF-12 with a not-to-exceed estimate.

periods.analysis: This is the first red quarter, driven by Tidal & Storm Flooding Events rising from 28 to 30 days against the <=20-day target. Water Main Breaks climbed from 14.2 to 14.9 breaks/100mi, still green but too close to the rail for a system with 185,000 residents and airport/seaport demand riding on it. Unplanned Outage Minutes improved slightly from 40 to 39 minutes, and Non-Revenue Water moved from 11.1% to 11.2%, so operations are still containing the customer impact. The concern is managed, but the pattern says we need to stop treating aging mains and tidal flooding as separate conversations; they meet in the same saturated trenches.
periods.recommendations: Activate the Pipeline Renewal candidate list now, starting with asbestos-cement segments WM-12-203 and WM-12-219 in the North Harbor pressure zone, and complete potholing before the Q2 paving window closes. Keep the outage playbook that brought minutes down to 39 minutes, including pre-staged clamps at Yard B and police-assisted traffic control on arterial breaks. Assign Stormwater to produce a two-week tide-event after-action report for the 30 rolling days, with each closure linked to an outfall, pump, or inlet asset ID.

periods.analysis: The red status holds, and now the water main trend has crossed the target: Water Main Breaks increased from 14.9 to 15.6 breaks/100mi, moving from green to yellow against <=15. Unplanned Outage Minutes rose from 39 to 41 minutes but remains green, and Non-Revenue Water moved from 11.2% to 11.3%, also green. Tidal & Storm Flooding Events increased again from 30 to 32 days, still red, with the highest call volume on the Seaport Connector and Old Ferry Road during back-to-back spring tides. The crews are doing good field work; the assets are old enough that good field work is no longer a substitute for renewal.
periods.recommendations: Advance Pipeline Renewal Package PR-25A by 60 days for the 8-inch cast-iron runs on Old Ferry Road, including WM-09-061 through WM-09-074, and bundle restoration with the resurfacing contract. Sustain the green outage performance by keeping bypass hose kits and insertion valves assigned to Crew 1 and Crew 4 rather than returning them to central stores. For the 32 flooding days, deploy inlet vacuuming on the Dock Street, Old Ferry, and Seaport Connector routes before each forecast coastal storm and track cleared cubic yards by route.

periods.analysis: The system is still red, with every movement except outage containment going the wrong way. Water Main Breaks rose from 15.6 to 16.3 breaks/100mi, Unplanned Outage Minutes increased from 41 to 42 minutes but stayed green, Non-Revenue Water moved from 11.3% to 11.5% and stayed green, and Tidal & Storm Flooding Events rose from 32 to 34 days. Summer soil movement showed up in the break map, especially along the 1960s cast iron in the Bayview and North Harbor grids, while the seaport lowlands took another round of tide-backed stormwater. This is concerned-but-managed: customers are mostly staying in service, but the asset curve is bending the wrong way.
periods.recommendations: Lock Pipeline Renewal PR-25A into construction notice and add PR-25B design for Bayview mains WM-14-088 to WM-14-103, using break frequency, pipe age, and leak noise as the ranking evidence. Keep the outage metric green by continuing 24-hour restoration coverage on airport and hospital feeders and testing the portable generator at Booster Station BS-3 every Friday. Extend the tide response by adding two temporary level sensors at OF-7 and OF-19 so the 34-day flooding count is backed by depth and duration, not just calls.

periods.analysis: This quarter is a harder red because Water Main Breaks increased from 16.3 to 17 breaks/100mi and moved from yellow to red. Unplanned Outage Minutes rose from 42 to 43 minutes but remains green, and Non-Revenue Water increased from 11.5% to 11.7%, still under the <=12% target. Tidal & Storm Flooding Events moved from 34 to 36 days, red again, with king-tide closures forcing detours around Terminal Gate 3 and the lower blocks of Harbor Avenue. The crew response is disciplined, but the pipes are telling us the renewal clock is no longer theoretical.
periods.recommendations: Treat Pipeline Renewal as a reliability program, not a beautification project: issue notice to proceed on PR-25A and finish 90% design on PR-25B with alternates for night work near Terminal Gate 3. Sustain the still-green Non-Revenue Water result by keeping district meter calibration on DMAs 4, 7, and 9 and escalating any night-flow increase over 8% to same-week leak investigation. Put a temporary flood barrier and pump package on Harbor Avenue for the winter season and document avoided closure hours for the AA-rated capital plan discussion.

periods.analysis: The red condition deepened this quarter: Water Main Breaks climbed from 17 to 18 breaks/100mi, and Unplanned Outage Minutes jumped from 43 to 50 minutes, moving from green to yellow. Non-Revenue Water increased from 11.7% to 11.9% but remains green by a thin margin, while Tidal & Storm Flooding Events rose from 36 to 37 days and remains red. The January freeze-thaw cycle found weak joints on WM-14-096 and WM-09-068, and one repair window ran long because the 12-inch valve at V-14-221 would not fully seat. This is not a panic situation, but it is a controlled failure trend, which is exactly what Pipeline Renewal is meant to arrest.
periods.recommendations: Move Pipeline Renewal PR-25A into double-shift work on the Old Ferry Road segment and authorize long-lead valves for PR-25B before bid opening, so procurement does not become the schedule. Recover outage performance by replacing or rebuilding the non-seating valves V-14-221, V-09-144, and V-08-117 and running a tabletop shutdown drill for the airport pressure zone. Preserve the 11.9% Non-Revenue Water result by adding weekend leak-correlation patrols after pressure transients and by reviewing meter alarms every Monday morning.

periods.analysis: The latest quarter stays red and adds a new warning light: Water Main Breaks increased from 18 to 19 breaks/100mi, Unplanned Outage Minutes rose from 50 to 54 minutes, and Non-Revenue Water moved from 11.9% to 12.8%, shifting from green to yellow. Tidal & Storm Flooding Events also increased from 37 to 38 days, still red against the <=20-day target. The break cluster is now concentrated enough to be actionable, with repeated failures on the North Harbor cast-iron grid and service interruptions lengthened by traffic control around seaport freight routes. The good news is that the evidence is clean; the bad news is that it points to the same answer in feet of pipe, valves, and outfalls.
periods.recommendations: Rebaseline Pipeline Renewal with a 24-month replacement target for the North Harbor and Old Ferry Road clusters, publish the asset list by ID, and bring the first change order only if it buys measurable break reduction. Pull Non-Revenue Water back below 12% by auditing large meters at the airport, seaport, and hospital accounts and pressure-testing DMAs 4, 7, and 9 after midnight when demand is low. For flooding, accelerate permanent backflow prevention at OF-12 and OF-19 while keeping temporary pumps on Dock Street until the 38-day rolling count starts to turn.

periods.analysis: September performance remains below plan, with water and sewer main breaks reaching 20 per 100 miles. The results point to continued reliability challenges in aging infrastructure and reinforce the need to prioritize investments based on pipe condition, break history, and service-impact data.
periods.recommendations: Use the pipe-cohort findings and outage records to sequence Phase 3 work. Report water loss and flooding separately, and retain temporary protections until permanent assets are commissioned and results improve.
